incoming.anchor: geology of the Grand Canyon area
incoming.excerpt: This and later study by geologists uncovered the geology of the Grand Canyon area and helped to advance that science.

outgoing.name: Arthropod
outgoing.excerpt: Also fossilized are arthropod and early reptile tracks along with some burrows.

outgoing.name: Fern
outgoing.excerpt: Fossils of winged insects, cone-bearing plants, and ferns are found in this formation as well as tracks of amphibians and reptiles.

outgoing.name: Insect
outgoing.excerpt: Fossils of winged insects, cone-bearing plants, and ferns are found in this formation as well as tracks of amphibians and reptiles.

outgoing.name: Invertebrate
outgoing.excerpt: Shark teeth have been found in this formation as well abundant fossils of marine invertebrates such as brachiopods, corals, mollusks, sea lilies, and worms.

outgoing.name: Plant
outgoing.excerpt: Fossils include amphibian footprints, reptiles, and plentiful plant material in the eastern part and increasing numbers of marine fossils in the western part.

outgoing.name: Reptile

outgoing.name: Shark

outgoing.name: Trout
outgoing.section: Recent geology, human impact, and the future
outgoing.excerpt: Once both muddy and warm, with only bottom feeding fish, the river is now clear and cold and now supports planted trout.

outgoing.name: Worm
outgoing.excerpt: Fossils of trilobites and burrowing worms are common in these formations.
